v.rationale: All three pass their own suites (13, 12 and 11 tests). The core logic is nearly identical: a grouped whereNull/orWhere scope written with #[Scope], and the new console attributes. Probes showed identical behaviour on the edge cases: --days=0, '', '+5', ' 5', '05', '1e2' and a very large value (all three reject '05'). What separates them is the requirement that 'the number shows up in our logs'. impl-2 schedules the command with no output destination, and the probe showed the event's output is /dev/null, so the requirement is not met. That is the only real bug found. impl-1 and impl-3 both append the output to storage/logs/inactive-users.log. impl-1 ranks first: it has the strongest tests (frozen time, the exact-cutoff boundary, empty --days, never-logged-in users), simple filter_var validation and an index on the column. Its weakness is a bare-number log line with no context. impl-3 is correct but has weaker tests (no frozen time, no boundary test, a vague 'days' assertion), heavier Validator ceremony, and the '1 users' pluralisation slip. impl-2 has the best output message and very good tests but misses a stated requirement, so it ranks last.
